scholarships.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Short-term Program for North American and European Researchers, PE)
scholarships.official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), Overseas Fellowship Division, International Program Department

existing.description: This programme brings PhD students and PhD researchers from North America and Europe to Japan to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of a Japanese host for between one and twelve months. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders or JPY200,000 per month for non-PhD holders at the start of the research in Japan, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 for fellows with three or more months of tenure, and overseas travel insurance. A research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses is applied for by the host researcher. The award is a research fellowship, not a degree scholarship, so no tuition is funded.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an eligible country, or have been engaged in research continuously for at least three years at a university or research institution in an eligible country (eligible countries: US, Canada, EU countries, UK, Switzerland, Norway and Russia); Taiwan and Palestine are also treated as eligible

Have obtained a doctoral degree from a foreign graduate school and, as of April 1 of the fiscal year, be within six years of having obtained that degree, or be currently enrolled in a doctoral course at a foreign graduate school and expect to receive a Ph.D. within two years from the start date of the fellowship period
Whether or not the candidate is employed in a full-time position is not considered

Researchers who have continuously carried out research for three or more years, or obtained their PhD within six years, minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks counted as one month)
A person who has never engaged in research at universities etc. in Japan would be most preferable

Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard (P), Short-term (PE), Short-term (PA), or Pathway to University positions in Japan (PU)) are not eligible
Those who have resident cards with mailing addresses in Japan at the application deadline set by JSPS are not eligible
A Japanese citizen who is also a permanent resident of an eligible country is not eligible
A selected fellow needs to submit an original copy of the doctoral degree certificate or diploma, or the prospect certificate if the degree is not yet obtained, before the fellowship starting date
The host researcher must be a full-time researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution and may submit up to three applications
existing.eligibility_summary: Candidates resident in an eligible North American or European country who obtained a doctoral degree within the past six years as of April 1 of the fiscal year, or who are enrolled in a doctoral course and expect a PhD within two years of the fellowship start date.
benefits: The settling-in allowance applies only to fellows with three or more months of tenure
Airfare outbound and the settling-in allowance are not paid to a candidate who has been living in Japan with a mailing address before the fellowship start date
Three application periods a year give flexibility in timing
coverage: Maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders
Maintenance allowance of JPY200,000 per month for candidates who are not PhD holders when research starts in Japan
Round-trip air ticket (based on JSPS regulations)
Settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 for fellows with three or more months of tenure
Research support allowance to cover cooperative research-related expenses, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
Submit the application form using the JSPS Electronic Application System by the deadline designated by the host institution, which may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline
The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before the application periods set by JSPS
The host institution must verify approval by the head of the institution and that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved
documents: FORM1 (Reference): application form for the JSPS Electronic Application System, completed by the host researcher
FORM2: application form completed by the foreign candidate (Short-term version)
Letter of Recommendation (Sample): one-page letter of recommendation from the candidate's recommender, written in English or in Japanese
application_method: Confirm your country of residence or citizenship is in the eligible list
Secure a host researcher at an eligible Japanese institution who is willing to apply for you
Check the host institution's internal deadline, which may precede the JSPS deadline by more than a month
Complete the Short-term FORM2 and obtain a one-page recommendation letter
Host researcher submits through the JSPS Electronic Application System and the institution transmits to JSPS
existing.best_fit: PhD candidates and PhD researchers based in the US, Canada, EU countries, the UK, Switzerland, Norway or Russia who have not previously done research at a Japanese university and can arrange a Japanese host.
existing.notes: Country eligibility is strict: applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of the US, Canada, EU countries, UK, Switzerland, Norway or Russia, or have three or more continuous years of research at an institution in one of those countries. The published page does not state any language test score requirement, so treat English proficiency as an inferred practical need rather than a published criterion. The settling-in allowance is conditional on a tenure of three or more months. Airfare and settling-in support are withheld from candidates already resident in Japan.
existing.application_period: Three open calls per year. FY2027 2nd: application deadline January 8, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results mid-May 2027, arrival August 1, 2027 - March 31, 2028, 20 fellowships. FY2027 3rd: application deadline June 4, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results late September 2027, arrival December 1, 2027 - March 31, 2028, 20 fellowships. The JSPS Electronic Application System opens approximately two months before each period.
existing.deadline_display: FY2027 2nd recruitment: January 8, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 3rd recruitment: June 4, 2027, 5 p.m. JST. The FY2027 1st recruitment closed on September 25, 2026.

scholarships.title: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme) - Cycle 2026
scholarships.official_source: UNESCO, funded by the Government of Japan under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources

existing.funding_period: one-time lump sum, up to the published ceiling
existing.description: Under the 2026 cycle UNESCO and the Government of Japan award 10 fellowships to young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye to carry out postgraduate research in a Japanese university or research institution. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence in Japan including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses, and other research-related expenses where applicable. It is a research fellowship, not a degree programme: the grant does not cover tuition fees, and the page publishes no award figures beyond the US$10,000 ceiling.
eligibility: Be nationals of one of the invited Member States or Associate Members listed in Annex 1
Be no more than 40 years old at the time of application
Hold at least a Master's degree or equivalent in a field relevant to the proposed research and demonstrate strong academic and research potential
Demonstrate sufficient proficiency in reading and writing in the language of instruction or supervision at the proposed host institution in Japan
Have obtained acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, who will oversee the proposed research
existing.eligibility_summary: National of an invited Member State or Associate Member, aged no more than 40 at the time of application, holding at least a Master's degree or equivalent relevant to the proposed research, proficient in the language of instruction or supervision at the Japanese host institution, and already accepted by an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution.
benefits: Medical insurance is mandatory for all selected fellows and is arranged by UNESCO on their behalf, with the cost deducted from the total fellowship amount before disbursement
Research stays in Japanese universities and research institutions, from February 2027 onwards and to be completed no later than December 2027
coverage: International and domestic travel for the approved itinerary
Personal subsistence in Japan, including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses
requirements: Read carefully the Application Guide to understand the requirements for eligible candidatures and the procedures for the submission of application
Contact the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country to enquire about the application procedures at the national level

Prepare all required documents, including the application form (Annex 3), academic documents, recommendation letter, host institution acceptance letter, language certificate and research proposal (Annex 4)
Submit your application to the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country at least 2 weeks before the required deadline
Once nominated by your National Commission, send the online application form and supporting documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org
Only applications nominated by the National Commission will be accepted by UNESCO
The research proposal must fall within one of the five listed research areas, selecting one primary research area and one corresponding sub-area from Annex 2
application_method: Contact the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country to learn the national procedures
Obtain acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution
Prepare the application form, academic documents, recommendation letter, host institution acceptance letter, language certificate and research proposal
Submit everything to your National Commission for UNESCO at least 2 weeks before the deadline
When your National Commission nominates you, send the online application form and supporting documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org
existing.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by a Selection Committee composed of experts from UNESCO and the Government of Japan in the relevant fields, taking into account the merits of the candidates and the quality, relevance and originality of their proposed research. The final selection decision is made by the Japanese authorities based on the recommendation of the Committee, with due consideration to gender equality and diversity.
existing.best_fit: Researchers aged 40 or under who hold at least a Master's degree (or equivalent) in a field relevant to the proposed research, come from an invited Member State or Associate Member, already have acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, and are applying in one of the five listed research areas on heritage conservation, AI for natural resources and climate action, ethical and human-centred AI, AI for sustainable cities and infrastructure, or AI and education.
existing.notes: Only 10 fellowships are awarded in the 2026 cycle, and only applications nominated by your National Commission are accepted, so the national shortlist is the binding gate. The fellowship grant is a lump sum capped at US$10,000, not a line-itemed scholarship, and the cost of the mandatory medical insurance is deducted from the total before disbursement, so the amount actually received is below the ceiling. The grant does NOT cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment including computers, publication costs, or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project. Candidates who submit incomplete applications, or who submit the online applications beyond the deadline, will not be considered. The practical deadline is at least two weeks earlier than 15 October 2026 because your National Commission must forward the file.
existing.duration: No less than 3 months and no more than 9 months
existing.application_period: Cycle 2026 call is open (page last updated 28 September 2026, stating the application for the Cycle 2026 is open and the deadline is now extended to 15 October 2026). Because the National Commission needs at least two weeks, the practical national deadline falls around 1 October 2026. Fellowship period in Japan from February 2027 onwards, to be completed no later than December 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Deadline for candidate submission is now extended to 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time. Letters of nomination and all application documents must reach UNESCO from the National Commissions no later than 15 October 2026, and candidates must submit to their own National Commission at least 2 weeks before the required deadline.
existing.program_type: UN agency research fellowship (UN and government co-sponsored)
